description: FIRST CIRCULAR-PATTERN GOLDEN (engineering-audit F4 — the one shipped body-affecting op with only an in-process volume unit test and NO golden / no cross-interpreter determinism gate; it is also the rotation/trig-heaviest op, so it had the weakest determinism coverage of anything shipped). A 10x10 mm square sketched on the XY datum plane (the quadrant-1 corner at the origin), extruded 10 mm into the unit prism [0,10]^3, then CIRCULAR-PATTERNED about the world +Z axis through the origin with angle 360 deg and count 4 (total instances incl. the seed). A three-feature TREE (sketch -> extrude -> circular pattern) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as every other golden. Semantics (design 7.6, docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md 2026-07-12): a pattern replicates the CURRENT body and BOOLEAN-UNIONS the copies into the single body chain. Instances are placed every angle_deg/count = 90 deg for k=1..count-1 (the closing position at 360 deg is EXCLUSIVE), so the four copies land in the four coordinate quadrants and TILE the square [-10,10] x [-10,10] x [0,10] meeting face-to-face on the x=0 and y=0 planes — proving the fuse ran AND merged the four quadrant prisms into ONE connected solid (a disjoint result would be a pattern_disjoint error). Locks: the circular-pattern handler + rotation placement math (Axis rotate by 90/180/270 deg) + incremental fuse + single-solid finalize, GProp over the fused box, exact topology after clean(), and (via the parametrized gates) in-process + interpreter-restart byte-determinism and STEP round-trip of the patterned body. This is the F4 determinism gate: the trig-heaviest op now rides the cross-interpreter byte-identity gate every other feature rides.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The seed body is the quadrant-1 unit prism: the 10x10 square (corners (0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(0,10) on XY; 4 corner coincidences + horizontal e1 + vertical e2 + distance e1=10 + distance e2=10, zero residual) extruded 10 mm along +Z = the box [0,10] x [0,10] x [0,10]. The sketch is underconstrained (position DOF remain) with zero initial residual, so planegcs provably returns the input positions bitwise (same solver posture as the extrude/linear-pattern goldens); the extrude is the box golden's construction path.

pattern: circular, axis through the origin (0,0,0) along +Z (0,0,1), angle 360 deg, count 4 -> step = 360/4 = 90 deg. Instance 0 is the seed at x,y in [0,10] (quadrant 1). Instance 1 is rotated +90 deg about +Z: (x,y) -> (-y,x), mapping [0,10]x[0,10] to [-10,0]x[0,10] (quadrant 2). Instance 2 is rotated +180 deg: (x,y) -> (-x,-y) -> [-10,0]x[-10,0] (quadrant 3). Instance 3 is rotated +270 deg: (x,y) -> (y,-x) -> [0,10]x[-10,0] (quadrant 4). The four unit-square prisms tile the square [-10,10] x [-10,10] with identical z in [0,10] and meet face-to-face along the x=0 and y=0 planes, so the fuse yields a single connected solid: the box [-10,10] x [-10,10] x [0,10].

volume = 20 * 20 * 10 = 4000 mm^3. Unlike the linear-pattern golden (spacing 6 < width 10, so consecutive copies OVERLAP in volume and the union counts overlap once), the four circular quadrants share only ZERO-MEASURE boundary faces (no volumetric overlap), so here union volume = count * seed = 4 * 1000 = 4000 mm^3 EXACTLY.
surface_area = 2*(20*20) + 4*(20*10) = 800 (top+bottom, normal to Z) + 800 (four 20x10 sides) = 1600 mm^2 (a 20x20x10 rectangular prism).

centroid = (0, 0, 5) mm by the 4-fold rotational symmetry of the four quadrants about the +Z axis (x=y=0) and mid-height (z=5). The axis passes exactly through the centroid in x,y -- a strong check that the 90/180/270 deg rotations placed the copies symmetrically (a biased trig error would pull the centroid off the axis).
bounding_box = [-10,-10,0]..[10,10,10]: the union spans x,y in [-10,10] (quadrant corners reach +/-10 on each axis) and z in [0,10] unchanged by rotation about +Z.

topology: the union of the four axis-aligned quadrant prisms is a single rectangular box -> 6 planar faces, 12 straight edges, 1 closed shell. clean() merges the four coplanar top squares into one top face (and likewise the bottom), collapses the interior x=0 and y=0 walls, and joins each pair of collinear outer wall segments into one 20x10 side -> an UNMERGED union would show interior walls and split faces, so this exact count proves the fuse+clean collapsed the seams.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default): each planar rectangular face tessellates to exactly 2 triangles (6 faces * 2 = 12 triangles); faceted per-face normals mean no vertex sharing across faces, so 6 faces * 4 corners = 24 vertices (same convention as the box-10x20x30, sketch-extrude, and linear-pattern goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Unlike the linear-pattern golden's axis-aligned +X translation (deviations EXACTLY 0.0), the circular pattern places copies via 90/180/270 deg rotations whose cos/sin are NOT floating-point-exact, so a small non-zero residual is expected and honest. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-12, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume |3999.999999999999 - 4000| ~ 1.1e-12, surface_area ~ 4.5e-13, centroid.x ~ 3.9e-16 (essentially on-axis), centroid.z ~ 9e-16, AABB bounds ~ 2e-15. Documented ceiling 1e-9 covers the worst measured residual (~1.1e-12, the volume) with ~1000x headroom for libm/BLAS/platform trig variation across CI hosts, while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 kernel bound and matching the linear-pattern/box goldens' 1e-9 posture -- there justified by exact-zero translation, here by measured trig residual. Topology and mesh counts carry NO tolerance (exact-match). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
